because of your fury and your anger;
for you have lifted me up and thrown me away.

My days are like an evening shadow stretching out;
like grass I dry up.

But you, Yahweh, are enthroned forever;
your renown lasts through all generations.

For your servants hold her stones dear
and pity her dust.

Nations will fear the name of Yahweh,
and all the kings of the earth your glory.

For Yahweh has built up Zion;
he has been seen in his glory.

He will turn to the prayer of the destitute
and will not despise their plea.

Let this be written down for a later generation,
so that a people yet to be created may praise Yah:

that he gazed down from his sanctuary on high;
Yahweh looked from heaven to the earth,

to hear the groans of prisoners,
to set free those condemned to die,

so that the name of Yahweh may be declared in Zion,
and his praise in Jerusalem,

when peoples gather together,
and kingdoms, to serve Yahweh.

He has humbled my strength on the road;{b}
he has shortened my days.

I say, “My God, do not take me away
in the middle of my days—
you whose years go on through all generations!

Long ago you founded the earth,
and the heavens are the work of your hands.{c}

but you are he who is,
and your years have no end.

The children of your servants will dwell secure,
and their offspring will be established before you.”

notes.text: The identification of these birds is uncertain.
So the qere; the ketiv reads “his strength.”
Verses 25–27 are quoted in Hebrews 1:10–12.

chapters.title: Of David.

verses.text:
Bless Yahweh, my soul,
and all that is within me, bless his holy name!

Bless Yahweh, my soul,
and forget none of his kindnesses—

who pardons every one of your iniquities,
who cures every one of your sicknesses,

who buys back your life from the pit,
who sets a crown on you of covenant love and compassion,

who satisfies your years{a} with good,
so that your youth is renewed like the eagle’s.

Yahweh does righteous deeds
and justice for all the oppressed.

He made his ways known to Moses,
his deeds to the people of Israel.

Yahweh is compassionate and gracious,
slow to anger and rich in covenant love.{b}

He will not always accuse,
nor will he hold on to his anger forever.

He has not treated us as our sins deserve,
nor repaid us according to our iniquities.

For as high as the heavens are above the earth,
so mighty is his covenant love toward those who fear him;

as far as the sunrise is from the sunset,
so far has he removed our transgressions from us.

As a father has compassion on his children,
so Yahweh has compassion on those who fear him.

For he knows what we are made of;
he keeps in mind that we are dust.

Man—his days are like the grass;
like a wildflower, so he blossoms;

when the wind passes over it, it is gone,
and its place no longer recognizes it.

But the covenant love of Yahweh is from everlasting to everlasting
on those who fear him,
and his righteousness to children’s children,

for those who hold to his covenant
and keep his precepts in mind to do them.

Yahweh has set up his throne in the heavens,
and his kingdom rules over all.

Bless Yahweh, you his angels,
mighty in strength, who carry out his word,
obeying the voice of his word!

Bless Yahweh, all his hosts,
his ministers who carry out his desire!

Bless Yahweh, all his works,
in every place of his dominion!
Bless Yahweh, my soul!

notes.text: The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain; traditionally “your mouth.”
Compare Exodus 34:6.

verses.text:
Bless Yahweh, my soul!
Yahweh my God, you are very great!
You are clothed with splendor and majesty,

wrapping yourself in light as in a robe,
stretching out the heavens like a tent curtain.

he makes the winds his messengers,
flames of fire his servants.{a}

He fixed the earth on its bases,
so that it will not totter, forever and ever.

You covered it with the deep as with a garment;
the waters stood above the mountains.

They fled from your rebuke;
they ran in haste at your thunder’s voice.

The mountains rose, the valleys sank{b}
to the place you had appointed for them.

You set a boundary they may not cross,
so that they never again cover the earth.

You make springs gush out in the valleys;
they flow between the hills;

they give drink to every animal of the field;
the wild donkeys quench their thirst.

Beside them the birds of the heavens nest;
they sing among the branches.

From your upper rooms you water the mountains;
the earth is satisfied with the fruit of your work.

You cause grass to sprout for the livestock
and plants for the labor of mankind,
so that bread comes out of the earth,

and wine that gladdens the heart of man,
oil to make his face shine,
and bread that strengthens the heart of man.

The trees of Yahweh drink their fill,
the cedars of Lebanon that he planted,

There the birds make their nests;
the stork lives in the junipers.

The high mountains are for the wild goats;
the rocks are a refuge for the rock badgers.{c}

He made the moon for the set times;{d}
the sun knows its hour for going down.

You bring darkness, and it is night,
when all the beasts of the forest prowl.

Young lions roar after prey
and ask God for their food.

The sun comes up, and they slip away
to lie down in their lairs.

Man goes out to his work
and to his labor until evening.

There is the sea, great and wide,
teeming with creatures beyond number,
living things both small and great.

There ships go back and forth,
and Leviathan, whom you shaped to frolic there.{e}

All of them look to you
to give them their food in its season.

You give to them, and they gather;
you open your hand, and they are filled with good.

When you send out your Spirit,{f} they are created,
and you renew the face of the ground.

May the glory of Yahweh last forever;
may Yahweh rejoice in his works,

He looks on the earth, and it quakes;
he touches the mountains, and smoke rises!

I will sing to Yahweh all my life;
I will make music to my God as long as I live.

May my meditation be pleasing to him;
as for me, I rejoice in Yahweh.

Let sinners vanish from the earth,
and let the wicked be no more!
Bless Yahweh, my soul!
Hallelujah!{g}

notes.text: Or “he makes his angels winds.” Quoted in Hebrews 1:7.
Or “They went up the mountains and went down into the valleys.”
Hebrew shephanim, the rock hyrax.
Or “the appointed festivals.”
Or “to play with.” Compare Job 41:5.
Or “your breath.”

Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” Yah is a short form of the name Yahweh. This is the first occurrence of the word in the Bible; it recurs in Psalms 105–106, 111–113, 115–117, 135, and 146–150, and in Revelation 19:1–6. CJT keeps the familiar transliteration “Hallelujah.”

verses.text:
Give thanks to Yahweh; call on his name;{a}
make his deeds known among the peoples!

Sing to him, make music to him;
ponder all his wonders!

Take pride in his holy name;
may the hearts that seek Yahweh rejoice!

Search for Yahweh and his strength;
seek his face always!

Remember the wonders he has worked,
his signs, and the judgments he has spoken,

you offspring of Abraham, his servant,
you children of Jacob, his chosen ones!

He is Yahweh our God;
his judgments are in all the earth.

He remembers his covenant forever,
the word he decreed for a thousand generations,

the covenant he made with Abraham,
his sworn promise to Isaac,

He made it firm for Jacob as an ordinance,
an everlasting covenant for Israel,

declaring, “The land of Canaan I give to you,
your allotted inheritance.”

When they were few in number,
a mere handful, and foreigners in it,

wandering from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to another people,

he let no one oppress them;
he rebuked kings on their account:

“Do not touch my anointed ones,
and do my prophets no harm!”

He summoned a famine on the land
and broke every staff of bread.{b}

Ahead of them he had sent a man:
Joseph, sold into slavery.

They hurt his feet with shackles;
his neck{c} was put in iron,

until the time that his word came true;
the word of Yahweh tested him.

The king gave the order to loose him;
the one who ruled the peoples released him.

He made him lord over his household
and ruler over all his possessions,

to bind his princes at his will
and to teach his elders wisdom.

Israel then entered Egypt;
Jacob stayed as an alien in Ham’s land.{d}

And God made his people very fruitful
and made them stronger than their foes.

He turned their hearts to hate his people,
to deal craftily with his servants.

He sent Moses, his servant,
and Aaron, whom he had chosen.

They performed his signs among them,{e}
and wonders in the land of Ham.

He sent darkness and made it dark;
did they not rebel against his words?{f}

He turned their waters into blood
and made their fish die.

Their land swarmed with frogs,
even in the rooms of their kings.

He spoke, and swarms of flies came,
and gnats throughout their territory.

He gave them hail in place of rain,
and flashes of fire throughout their land.

He battered their vines and their fig trees
and splintered the trees throughout their borders.

He spoke, and the locusts came,
young locusts without number,

which devoured all the vegetation in their land
and ate up the fruit of their ground.

He struck down every firstborn in their land,
the first fruits of all their vigor.

Then he brought Israel out with silver and gold,
and among his tribes no one stumbled.

Egypt was glad when they left,
for dread of Israel had fallen on them.

He stretched a cloud over them for a screen
and fire to give light by night.

They made a request, and he sent quail,
and filled them with heaven’s bread.

He opened the rock, and water gushed out;
it ran through the dry land like a river.

For he remembered his holy word
to Abraham, his servant.

He led his people out rejoicing,
his chosen with songs of joy.

He gave them the lands of the nations,
and they took possession of what the peoples had toiled for,

That is, the food supply.
Hebrew nephesh, “his soul” or “his throat.” So the qere; the ketiv has “his foot” in the previous line.
A poetic name for Egypt; compare Genesis 10:6.
Hebrew “They set among them the words of his signs.”
So the qere (and the Septuagint and Syriac omit “not”: “they rebelled against his words”). The ketiv reads “his word.” The sense of the line is debated.

verses.text:
Who can tell of the mighty deeds of Yahweh
or make all his praise heard?

Happy are those who keep justice,
who do righteousness at all times!

Remember me, Yahweh, when you show favor to your people;
visit me with your salvation,

that I may see the prosperity of your chosen ones,
that I may rejoice in the gladness of your nation,
that I may boast along with your inheritance.

We have sinned, as our fathers did;
we have done wrong; we have acted wickedly.

Yet he saved them for the sake of his name,
to make his might known.

He rebuked the Red Sea, and it became dry;
he guided them through the depths as if through open country.

He saved them from the hand of the one who hated them
and redeemed them from the power of the enemy.

The waters closed over their foes;
not a single one survived.

Then they believed his words;
they sang his praise.

How soon they forgot what he had done!
They would not wait for his plan.

In the wilderness they were seized with greed
and tested God in the barren land.

So he granted their request,
yet he sent a wasting into their souls.

In the camp they grew jealous of Moses
and of Aaron, the holy one of Yahweh.

The earth opened and swallowed Dathan
and covered the company of Abiram.

Fire blazed out among their company;
flame burned up the wicked.

They made a calf at Horeb
and bowed down to a cast image.

They traded away their Glory{c}
for the likeness of a grass-eating bull.

They forgot God, their Savior,
who had done great things in Egypt,

wondrous works in the land of Ham,
awesome deeds at the Red Sea.

So he said he would destroy them—
had not Moses, his chosen one,
stood in the breach before him,
to turn his wrath away from destroying them.

Then they scorned the desirable land;
they put no faith in his promise.

They muttered in their tents
and would not heed Yahweh’s voice.

So he lifted his hand to them in an oath
to bring them down in the wilderness,

and make their offspring fall among the nations,
and scatter them throughout the lands.

They attached themselves to Baal of Peor
and ate offerings made to the dead.{d}

Their deeds provoked him to anger,
and plague burst out on them.

But Phinehas rose and stepped in to judge,
and the plague was held back.

It was credited to him as righteousness
for all generations, forever.

They angered him at the waters of Meribah,
and it went badly for Moses because of them,

because they made his spirit bitter,
and rash words came from his lips.

They did not destroy the peoples,
as Yahweh had commanded them,

but they intermingled with the nations
and adopted their ways.

They served their idols,
which became a snare to them.

They sacrificed their sons
and their daughters to demons.

They poured out innocent blood,
the blood of their sons and daughters,
whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan,
and the land was defiled with bloodshed.

So they became unclean by their deeds
and prostituted themselves in their practices.

Then the anger of Yahweh burned against his people,
and he loathed his own inheritance.

He gave them into the hand of the nations,
and those who hated them ruled over them.

Their enemies oppressed them,
and they were humbled under their power.

Many times he rescued them,
but they were rebellious in their plans
and sank low through their iniquity.

Yet he looked on their distress
when he heard their cry.

He called to mind his covenant for their sake
and had a change of heart in his abundant covenant love.{e}

He caused them to be pitied
by all who held them captive.

Save us, Yahweh our God!
Gather us out of the nations
to thank your holy name
and to take pride in praising you.

Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting!
And let all the people say, “Amen!”
Hallelujah!{f}

Hebrew Yam Suph, “Sea of Reeds,” here and in verses 9 and 22.
That is, God. An ancient scribal tradition records that the original reading was “my glory.”
Or “to lifeless gods.” Compare Numbers 25:1–9.
So the qere (plural, “his many acts of covenant love”); the ketiv is singular.
